observations.actual: [AC:spec-1-4] passed (exit 0). Read dispatch-start.mjs earlierReviews (skips reports not created after the last reopen) and dispatch-preflight.mjs (reviewer destination steps to the first free -r<n>).

findings.summary: The fresh round count after a reopen trusts the report's own createdAt: a report written after the reopen but stamped earlier is not counted, so the review limit relies on honest timestamps. Reopen itself needs a done PASS acceptance and a real byte change (a second reopen while in-review is refused, see probe receipt), so rounds cannot be reset without an accepted PASS in between.
findings.assumption: Reviewer-written timestamps are trusted elsewhere too; no blocking weakness.

findings.summary: The free report path is checked only in the worker root. In parallel mode an earlier report that exists only in the coordinator tree would not move the new path to -r<n>; earlierReviews looks in both roots.
findings.assumption: Serial and coordinator-tree reviews are the common case; spec does not decide the parallel case.

findings.summary: changedAcceptedInputs returns [] when the accepted report file is missing or unreadable, so submit gives no warning and reopen refuses with "no input changed" for that spec, instead of saying the report is missing.
A done dependent of a reopened spec stays done while its dependency is back in review; the spec does not say whether dependents should be flagged.
findings.assumption: Out of this spec; the submit warning covers changed bytes, not dependency status.
